newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB to build $45 mln Kenyan brewery.
newsitem.headline: SAB to build $45 mln Kenyan brewery.

text.p: Drinks giant South African Breweries Ltd, the world's fourth biggest brewer, said on Tuesday that it is to invest $45 million in building a new brewery in Kenya.

The new plant will be built at a greenfield site at Thika with a capacity of 800,000 hectolitres a year and will create 700 new jobs. SAB said the number of indirectly created jobs -- through supplier networks and retailers -- could be as many as 7,000.
The firm aims to have the brewery up and running by the end of next year, though staff recruitment and other preparations will begin immediately.
Ownership of the brewery will be split between Kenyan consortium Donyo Sabuk Holdings, Dutch development agency FMO and SAB.
Once the brewery has established a good track record it is aiming for a listing on the Nairobi Stock Exchange.
SAB said there was huge growth potential in Kenya.

"We believe that current beer consumption levels in Kenya are less than half of what they should be. There exists substantial room for growth in this market through the benefits of healthy competition," said SAB international division managing director Andre Parker.
SAB said the firm had got the necessary approvals for the transaction from the authorities of the relevant countries.
"We believe that the economic prospects for Kenya are excellent," Parker said.
SAB, which dominates its home South African market, has expanded rapidly abroad in recent years. The firm has breweries in Swaziland, Lesotho, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Tanzania and Zambia.
Outside Africa, the firm also has interests in Romania, Hungary, Poland and China.
